title: Compose a slug from references with andThen and compose

blocks.text: `f.andThen(g)` applies `f` first and then `g`; `f.compose(g)` applies `g` first and then `f`. A method reference has no type until it gets a target, so to call `andThen` on `String::trim` you first give it one, for example by assigning it to a `Function<String, String>` variable. A two-argument unbound reference such as `String::concat` fits a `BiFunction`, whose `andThen` takes a `Function`.

items: `Function<String, String> slug()` trims the text, lower-cases it and replaces each run of whitespace with one `-`.
`Function<String, Integer> slugLength()` gives the length of the slug of its argument. The page's way to build it is `String::length` composed with `slug()`.
`BiFunction<String, String, Integer> joinedLength()` gives the length of the two strings joined: `String::concat` and then `String::length`.

blocks.text: The order of the steps matters, and titles are not always spaced neatly.

cases.says: It turns a title into a slug, measures the slug, and measures two joined strings.
Trimming comes first in the chain, so outer spaces never become dashes.
A run of several spaces inside the title becomes a single dash.
slugLength measures the slug, so compose must run the slug function before String::length.

concepts: A two-argument unbound reference such as String::concat fits BiFunction, and its andThen chains a Function after it.
f.andThen(g) runs f first and f.compose(g) runs g first, so the chosen method fixes the order of the steps.
